claims.text: The as-cast alloy is a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The alloy initially has a naturally formed protective oxide film.
The initial oxide film is thermally stable.
Mechanical wear removes or disrupts the protective oxide film.
Oxide-film disruption exposes less stable, electrochemically active phases or intermetallic regions.
The exposed dissimilar phases form galvanic couples at phase boundaries.
Galvanic coupling between exposed phases intensifies localized corrosion.
Localized corrosion weakens the surface and makes it more susceptible to subsequent wear.
Corrosion-induced pits promote further mechanical wear.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion produce greater total degradation than either corrosion-only or wear-only exposure.
Combined exposure produces higher corrosion rates on newly exposed areas than the matched isolated-condition baselines.
Combined exposure produces deeper wear tracks than wear-only exposure.
The proposed mechanism requires wear sufficiently aggressive to remove the oxide film continuously.
The proposed mechanism requires an environment capable of supporting active corrosion.
The proposed mechanism is less likely or inactive at lower temperatures.
The proposed mechanism is less likely or inactive in an inert atmosphere.
The proposed mechanism is less likely or inactive when the mechanical load does not disturb the oxide film.
A three-arm experiment comparing corrosion-only, inert-atmosphere wear-only, and simultaneous wear-corrosion conditions is proposed.

contradictions.description: The controls are said to have identical environmental conditions, including corrosive-medium composition, while the wear-only control is also specified to use an inert, non-corrosive atmosphere. Those environmental conditions cannot literally be identical.
